title: Affine formal modules: Reconstruction
statement: Let A, I, B, X, J and the fixed canonical quotient functor Q be as in the statement dependencies. Let L be any functor from coherent formal J-modules to finite B-modules and p(F) a family of cones to the A-module towers Gamma(F_n). Assume the projections commute with maps L(f) and each nth projection is surjective with kernel I^(n+1)L(F) as an A-submodule. Then L followed by Q is naturally isomorphic to the identity on coherent formal J-modules. This conclusion does not assume that L is an equivalence, does not require a limiting cone or scalar equation, and asserts only the formal-system half of the equivalence.

proof.text: For each F and n, the first isomorphism theorem applied to its nth projection gives L(F)/I^(n+1)L(F) isomorphic to Gamma(F_n), with the isomorphism composed with the quotient map equal to p(F)_n. The assumed kernel equality and surjectivity are exactly its hypotheses.

The affine ideal-product/cokernel comparison identifies the nth component of Q(L(F)) with tilde of that module quotient. Coherence of F_n implies quasi-coherence, so the tilde/Gamma counit is an isomorphism to F_n. Compose with tilde of the preceding quotient isomorphism.

To check adjacent transition compatibility, precompose with the surjective quotient projection: both composites become the cone naturality equation for p(F). Cancel this projection. Every order arrow is a composite of adjacent arrows, so these components give an isomorphism of systems. To check naturality in F, precompose the same component square with the quotient projection; the assumed naturality of p and naturality of the tilde/Gamma counit identify the composites. Cancel again. Full-subcategory morphisms are exactly the ambient morphisms, so these natural isomorphisms lift to coherent formal systems, proving L followed by Q is identity up to natural isomorphism.

theorem coherentFormalModules_affine_reconstruction (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (J : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom))
    (L : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J ⥤
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N))
    (p : ∀ F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J,
      (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj
          (L.obj F).obj) ⟶ F.obj ⋙ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A))
    (hnatural : (∀ (F G : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (f : F ⟶ G)
      (n : ℕ),
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).map
        (L.map f).hom ≫ (p G).app (op n) =
      (p F).app (op n) ≫ (moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A)).map (f.hom.app (op n))))
    (hquotient : (∀ (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (n : ℕ),
      Function.Surjective ((p F).app (op n)) ∧
      LinearMap.ker ((p F).app (op n)).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj
            (L.obj F).obj)))) :
    Nonempty (L ⋙ (coherentFormalModules_affine_quotientFunctor A I J hJ) ≅ 𝟭 _)
